english.title: Threaten a person with a blade / sharply pointed article in a public place

additionalkeywords.additionalkeyword: Legal Aid Sentencing and punishment of offenders Act 2012

english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) had with you an article, namely **(..SPECIFY THE ARTICLE..), to which section 139AA of the Criminal Justice Act 1988 applied in a public place, namely **(..SPECIFY THE LOCATION..), and unlawfully and intentionally threatened another person, namely **(..SPECIFY THE PERSON..), with that article in such a way that there was an immediate risk of serious physical harm to that person

english.notes:
(i) "Public place" is defined in section 139(7) of the Criminal Justice Act 1988.
(ii) "Article" is defined in section 139(2) and (3) of the Criminal Justice Act 1988.
(iii) The court may find the defendant not guilty of this offence but guilty of an offence under section 139 or 139A of the Act.
(iv) The Offensive Weapons Act 2019 extended this offence, for offences committed on or after 6th April 2022 see H20302.

other.penalty:
Either way

Summary: maximum 12 months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: maximum 4 years imprisonment and / or a fine.

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.

The maximum penalty on summary conviction increased from 2nd May 2022. This applies only to offences committed on or after that date. For offences committed before 2nd May 2022 the maximum penalty on summary conviction is six months.

For minimum sentence for this offence see section 312 of the Sentencing Act 2020.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
